partner_context.their_ambition: As the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore you steward the world's busiest transshipment port and are driving its harbour craft to a clean-energy future — from 2030 every new harbour craft must be fully electric, B100-capable or net-zero-fuel ready, with net-zero harbour craft by 2050 under the Maritime Singapore Decarbonisation Blueprint.
partner_context.their_pressure: Singapore is land-constrained yet ringed by water, and the harbour-craft fleet still runs largely on diesel. The 2030 mandate needs credible, fast, clean-vessel options — not just slower battery retrofits — and the city needs new transport capacity it cannot build on land.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier makes electric the fast, premium option: a foiling standard MPA can prove first-of-class at home — on the harbour, the Southern Islands and a fast East Coast–CBD line — and export as a Singapore-led benchmark. The charging is already going in; the boat is the choice.

hero.eyebrow: Authority proposal · Republic of Singapore · Maritime & Port Authority
hero.title: The clean harbour-craft standard for Singapore
hero.subtitle: Singapore has already mandated cleaner harbour craft and built the first charging point. Navier makes the electric option the fast, premium, exportable one — across the harbour, the islands and the inner waterfront.

why_now: MPA's 2030 harbour-craft mandate gives explicit top-cover for a clean-vessel transition, and Singapore is one of the densest waterfront cities on earth. The first electric-harbour-craft charging point is already live at Marina South Pier, and MPA is selecting reference vessel designs. Foiling makes electric viable at speed — efficient per passenger-mile, smooth and near-silent — and the hybrid covers the longer cross-border legs with no charging dependency. This is the moment to set foiling as the clean standard.

It plugs into the MRT and bus network at shared interchanges, runs on the clean-craft berths and charging MPA is already building, and adds a fast East Coast–CBD line plus harbour and island services — new transport capacity for a land-constrained city, without adding a car to the road.

differentiation.headline: Built for public value
differentiation.body: This proposal is measured the way a maritime authority measures its mandate: harbour-craft emissions cut against the 2030 and 2050 targets, new transport capacity added for a land-constrained city, island and waterfront access widened, and a clean-harbour-craft standard proven first-of-class and exportable. It is a public network with a credible operating model — not a marketplace.

proof_points.claim: Singapore has already mandated clean harbour craft — fully electric, B100 or net-zero-fuel capable for all new craft from 2030, net-zero harbour craft by 2050.
proof_points.evidence: Maritime Singapore Decarbonisation Blueprint 2050; MPA harbour-craft electrification targets.

proof_points.claim: The first electric-harbour-craft charging point is live at Marina South Pier, and MPA has shortlisted clean-craft vessel designs.
proof_points.evidence: e-HC charging pilot (Pyxis + SP Mobility, 2024); 11 passenger-launch and lighter designs shortlisted; national charging masterplan in development.

proof_points.claim: The Johor–Singapore Causeway carries roughly 350,000 crossings a day — one of the busiest land borders on earth — and a marine relief corridor addresses real demand.
proof_points.evidence: Causeway crossing volumes; the JB–Singapore RTS Link opens end-2026 to ease congestion.

proof_points.claim: Domestic water transport already exists on slow craft — a foiling upgrade improves a live mode, not a novelty.
proof_points.evidence: Marina South Pier runs daily Southern-Islands ferries; Changi Point runs on-demand Pulau Ubin bumboats.

objections.a: Foiling cuts energy per passenger-mile dramatically, so electric range and speed both work — making the 2030 mandate practical rather than a compromise on performance.

objections.q: Charging infrastructure in a dense port?
objections.a: Pioneer II charges at existing piers — the Marina South Pier charging point is already live — and the Quanta-LR hybrid covers the longer cross-border legs with no new infrastructure.

objections.q: Wake and safety in one of the world's busiest ports?
objections.a: Foiling is software-governed: geofenced low-wake and no-foil zones in anchorages and fairways, automatic speed limits, and full pilotage compliance. The vessel foils only on cleared corridors — and a foiling hull throws far less wake at speed than today's planing craft.
Around public value — emissions cut, congestion relieved, capacity and access added — plus a transparent operating model. The exact fares, frequencies and cost-recovery are set with the authority.

the_ask: Partner with Navier on a clean-harbour-craft pilot: run foiling vessels on the Marina South Pier charging point and the Southern-Islands and East Coast–CBD corridors, produce the first-of-class data package MPA can stand behind and export, and scope optional cross-border relief corridors — all integrated with the MRT and bus network.
close: Singapore has already mandated cleaner harbour craft and built the first charging point. Navier gives MPA the fast, zero-emission, exportable standard that its harbour-craft transition is reaching for — domestic harbour and islands first, cross-border relief when Singapore is ready.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling is a genuine step-change in speed, comfort, wake and noise over conventional harbour craft — enough to make scheduled water transport a serious everyday mode in a dense, busy port.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: The first routes use what already exists: the live Marina South Pier charging point, the Southern-Islands and Pulau Ubin ferry jetties, and the Marina Bay water-taxi stops. Pioneer II charges at the pier; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging for the longer legs.
why_navier_now.the_moment: The 2030 mandate is set, the first charging point is live, and MPA is shortlisting clean harbour-craft designs. A foiling vessel is the fast, premium option that meets the mandate from day one — and the standard Singapore can export.

levers: Navier is the clean-harbour-craft standard MPA's 2030 mandate is reaching for. Foiling cuts energy per passenger-mile dramatically, so electric range and speed both work; it is near-silent and low-wake in a dense, busy port; and the Quanta-LR hybrid covers the longer cross-border legs with no charging dependency. Singapore is the ideal jurisdiction to prove it first-of-class and export the benchmark — starting with the domestic harbour and Southern-Islands network, with cross-border relief corridors as an optional second step.
Foiling makes the electric option fast and practical — the credible way to meet the 2030 mandate without compromising speed or range. MPA can prove it first-of-class at home and export the standard.
